claim: Complete genetic deficiency for the COPII component SEC24A is compatible with normal survival and development in the mouse.
source_text: We now report that complete genetic deficiency for the COPII component SEC24A is compatible with normal survival and development in the mouse, despite the fundamental role of SEC24 in COPII vesicle formation and cargo recruitment.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations from SEC24A-deficient mice showing normal survival and development as described in the Results section.

claim: SEC24A-deficient mice exhibit markedly reduced plasma cholesterol.
source_text: However, these animals exhibit markedly reduced plasma cholesterol
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental measurements of plasma cholesterol levels in SEC24A-deficient mice shown in Figure 3 and related data.

claim: Mutations in Apoe and Ldlr are epistatic to Sec24a.
source_text: with mutations in Apoe and Ldlr epistatic to Sec24a
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by genetic cross experiments showing that the hypocholesterolemia phenotype is abolished in Apoe and Ldlr deficient backgrounds.

claim: The hypocholesterolemia in SEC24A-deficient mice operates through a receptor-mediated lipoprotein clearance mechanism.
source_text: with mutations in Apoe and Ldlr epistatic to Sec24a, suggesting a receptor-mediated lipoprotein clearance mechanism.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the genetic epistasis data showing that LDLR and APOE mutations abolish the SEC24A phenotype, indicating the mechanism involves receptor-mediated clearance.

claim: Hepatic LDLR levels are up-regulated in SEC24A-deficient cells.
source_text: Consistent with these data, hepatic LDLR levels are up-regulated in SEC24A-deficient cells
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by immunoblotting data showing increased LDLR protein levels in SEC24A-deficient liver tissue.

claim: PCSK9 depends on SEC24A for efficient exit from the ER.
source_text: as a consequence of specific dependence of PCSK9, a negative regulator of LDLR, on SEC24A for efficient exit from the ER.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by in vitro COPII budding assays and measurements of plasma PCSK9 levels showing reduced secretion in SEC24A-deficient conditions.

claim: There is partial overlap in cargo selectivity between SEC24A and SEC24B.
source_text: Our findings also identify partial overlap in cargo selectivity between SEC24A and SEC24B
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experiments showing that depletion of both SEC24A and SEC24B has greater effects on PCSK9 packaging than depletion of SEC24A alone.

claim: Cargo selectivity heterogeneity in COPII vesicles extends to soluble as well as trans-membrane cargoes.
source_text: suggesting a previously unappreciated heterogeneity in the recruitment of secretory proteins to the COPII vesicles that extends to soluble as well as trans-membrane cargoes.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the finding that PCSK9, a soluble cargo, shows selective dependence on SEC24A, extending previous observations limited to transmembrane cargoes.

claim: One-third of the vertebrate genome is predicted to encode proteins that are sorted into the secretory pathway.
source_text: One-third of the vertebrate genome is predicted to encode proteins that are sorted into the secretory pathway en route to intracellular organelles, the cell surface, or the extracellular space
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Palade, 1975 and Bonifacino and Glick, 2004.

claim: Trans-membrane and soluble proteins synthesized in the ER are packaged into COPII-coated transport vesicles for export to the Golgi.
source_text: Following synthesis in the endoplasmic reticulum, trans-membrane and soluble proteins co-translationally inserted into the ER are packaged into transport vesicles coated with COPII (coat protein complex II) for export from the ER and delivery to the Golgi for further processing
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about the secretory pathway, supported by citation to Lee et al., 2004.

claim: COPII coat assembly is initiated at ER exit sites upon activation of the GTPase SAR1.
source_text: The assembly of the COPII coat is initiated at ER exit sites upon activation of the GTPase SAR1, which recruits the inner-coat heterodimer SEC23/SEC24, followed by the assembly of the outer-coat heterotetramer SEC13/SEC31 to generate carrier vesicles destined for the Golgi
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established mechanism of COPII assembly, supported by citations to Lee et al., 2004 and Gurkan et al., 2006.

claim: The SEC24 subunit of the COPII complex recognizes specific signals within cargo molecules.
source_text: A key sorting event in ER-Golgi transport relies on recognition of specific signals within cargo molecules by the SEC24 subunit of the COPII complex
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about SEC24 function, supported by multiple citations including Miller et al., 2002, 2003 and Lee et al., 2004.

claim: SEC23 may also contribute to cargo selection in some cases.
source_text: though SEC23 may also contribute to cargo selection in some cases
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2012.

claim: Mammals express multiple paralogous forms of COPII components.
source_text: Mammals express multiple paralogous forms of COPII, including two SAR1 GTPases (SAR1A/B), two SEC23s (SEC23A/B), four SEC24s (SEC24A-D), as well as two SEC31s (SEC31A/B)
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about mammalian COPII components, supported by citations to Wendeler et al., 2007 and Zanetti et al., 2011.

claim: The four mammalian SEC24 paralogs can be divided into two subfamilies, SEC24A/B and SEC24C/D, sharing ~60% sequence identity within but only ~25% identity across subfamilies.
source_text: The four mammalian SEC24 paralogs can be divided into two subfamilies, SEC24A/B and SEC24C/D, sharing ∼60% sequence identity within but only ∼25% identity across subfamilies
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about SEC24 sequence relationships, supported by citations to Mancias and Goldberg, 2008 and Zanetti et al., 2011.

claim: Mutations in human SAR1B result in chylomicron retention disease.
source_text: Mutations in human SAR1B result in chylomicron retention disease (Anderson Disease), a distinct defect in fat absorption due to reduced chylomicron assembly and secretion by intestinal enterocytes
evidence_reasoning: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citations to Jones et al., 2003 and Annesi et al., 2007.

claim: Missense mutations in human SEC23A result in a characteristic syndrome of malformations restricted to the craniofacial skeleton.
source_text: In contrast, missense mutations in human SEC23A result in a characteristic syndrome of malformations restricted to the craniofacial skeleton
evidence_reasoning: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citations to Boyadjiev et al., 2006, 2010.

claim: Mutations in human SEC23B result in congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II.
source_text: Mutations in human SEC23B result in the autosomal recessive disorder congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II, with abnormalities restricted to the hematopoietic erythroid compartment
evidence_reasoning: This is established clinical knowledge supported by citations to Bianchi et al., 2009 and Schwarz et al., 2009.

claim: SEC23B-deficient mice die at birth due to dramatic destruction of the pancreas.
source_text: Surprisingly, although red blood cells appear grossly normal in SEC23B-deficient mice, these animals die at birth due to dramatic destruction of the pancreas
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Tao et al., 2012.

claim: SEC24B deficiency in mice leads to failure in neural tube closure resulting from missorting of VANGL2.
source_text: SEC24B deficiency in mice leads to failure in neural tube closure resulting from missorting of the signaling molecule VANGL2
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Merte et al., 2010.

claim: Murine SEC24D deficiency results in very early embryonic lethality.
source_text: In contrast, murine SEC24D deficiency results in very early embryonic lethality

source_text: Sec24agt/gt mice were grossly indistinguishable from their wild type littermates and developed normally to adulthood with no difference in body weight on a normal or high fat diet

source_text: Gross and routine microscopic survey of multiple tissues failed to identify any obvious morphologic abnormalities in adult Sec24agt/gt mice

source_text: An ∼25kD protein (p25) is under-represented in the plasma of gt/gtSec24a mice.

claim: BFA treatment abolishes PCSK9 secretion into the medium and causes intracellular accumulation.

claim: PCSK9 is packaged into COPII vesicles in the presence of rat liver cytosol, ATP, and GTP.

claim: ER budding of PCSK9-containing vesicles is inhibited by GTPyS and constitutively active SAR1 (SAR1A H79G).

claim: Inhibition of COPII vesicle formation in cells by SAR1B H79G prevents secretion of PCSK9 into the medium.

claim: PCSK9 secretion is dependent on ER exiting in COPII-coated vesicles.

claim: PCSK9 co-immunoprecipitates with SEC24A and SEC24B but not with SEC24C or SEC24D.

claim: Over-expression of SEC24A or SEC24B enhances PCSK9 secretion.

claim: Depletion of both SEC24A and SEC24B has a greater effect on PCSK9 packaging than depletion of SEC24A alone.
source_text: and to a greater extent with depletion of both SEC24A and SEC24B

claim: Intrinsic cargo selectivity among SEC24 paralogs is a key determinant of SEC24 function.
source_text: Our data, together with those of Merte et al. (Merte et al., 2010), suggest that intrinsic cargo selectivity among SEC24 paralogs is a key determinant of SEC24 function.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the specific cargo dependencies observed for different SEC24 paralogs, combined with previous findings on VANGL2.

claim: VANGL2 specifically depends on SEC24B for ER exiting.
source_text: The latter authors demonstrated specific dependence of VANGL2, a key component of the planar cell polarity signaling pathway, on the SEC24B paralog for ER exiting

claim: PCSK9 is a specific SEC24A-dependent COPII cargo.
source_text: Our findings identify PCSK9 as a specific SEC24A-dependent COPII cargo.

claim: Loss of SEC24A disrupts PCSK9 secretion without affecting other COPII-dependent processes such as SREBP activation.

claim: SEC24A/B exhibit overlapping cargo specificities distinct from SEC24C/D.

claim: SEC24A/B are balanced in a cytoplasmic pool distinct from SEC24C/D.
source_text: These data imply that SEC24A/B are balanced in a cytoplasmic pool distinct from SEC24C/D.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the observation that SEC24B protein levels increase when SEC24A is absent, despite constant mRNA levels.

claim: There is extensive heterogeneity among COPII vesicles determined at least in part by SEC24 paralog composition.
source_text: our data raise the possibility of extensive heterogeneity among COPII vesicles and their function in cargo selection and export, determined at least in part by SEC24 paralog composition.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the diverse cargo specificities and functional differences observed among SEC24 paralogs.
